newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Investors talk on stake in Lithuania oil terminal.
newsitem.headline: Investors talk on stake in Lithuania oil terminal.

text.p: A group of foreign investors has started talks on buying a stake in the planned Butinge oil terminal in the Baltic state of Lithuania, a company official said on Thursday.

Project manager Ole Agerndal said that U.S. group Fluor Daniel, German Preussag, Russian Lukoil, the ARA company of Saudia Arabia and Omegon Petroleum Products were all interested in buying a stake in the terminal.
"We have had some very firm offers," Agerndal told Reuters.
The Butinge terminal has been on the drawing board for around two years and has been delayed due to funding problems.
The company plans to issue some 161.5 million litas in new shares to boost its share capital to 184.7 million litas.
Agerndal said that Butinge hopes investors will buy a 60 percent stake in the company's total share capital.

Construction of the terminal is expected to be completed by autumn 1998. Fluor and Preussag have already signed a letter of intent to complete the terminal, which is expected to have a total cost of some $200 million.
